en.g: Talk about art, museums and exhibitions with the right words.
p: Places and works: museum, gallery, exhibition, painting, portrait, landscape, sculpture, masterpiece.
Use the passive for who made it: The Starry Night was painted by Van Gogh. The Thinker was made by Rodin.
Give opinions: It's really striking. The colours are so vivid. I'm not really into abstract art.
en.q: Do you enjoy visiting museums or galleries? Which work of art has impressed you the most?
en.c: Describe a painting or sculpture you like in four sentences: what it shows, who made it and why you like it.

de.g: Du sprichst mit den richtigen Wörtern über Kunst, Museen und Ausstellungen.

Meinungen: It's really striking. The colours are so vivid. I'm not really into abstract art.

en.g: Describe photos clearly, saying where things are in the picture.
p: Position phrases: in the foreground, in the background, in the middle, on the left, on the right, at the top, at the bottom.
There is/are + place: There's a lighthouse on the right. There are some boats in the foreground.
Present continuous for actions: In the middle, a woman is taking a selfie. Two dogs are running on the beach.
en.q: Think of your favourite photo on your phone. What can you see in the foreground and in the background?
en.c: Describe one of your photos in five sentences using at least four different position phrases.

en.g: Speculate about a picture when you aren't sure what is happening.
p: Possible: They might be on holiday. It could be a wedding. Almost sure: It must be winter. Impossible: It can't be summer.
Look like + noun vs look + adjective: It looks like a market. They look happy. It seems to be very early.
Give a reason: She must be tired because she's yawning. They might be tourists, as they're holding a map.
en.q: Imagine a photo of people laughing at a table. Who might they be, and what could they be celebrating?
en.c: Find any picture and write four guesses about it with might, must, can't and looks like, each with a reason.

de.g: Du stellst Vermutungen über ein Bild an, wenn du nicht sicher bist, was passiert.
p: Möglich: They might be on holiday. It could be a wedding. Fast sicher: It must be winter. Unmöglich: It can't be summer.
Look like + Nomen vs. look + Adjektiv: It looks like a market. They look happy. It seems to be very early.
Begründe: She must be tired because she's yawning. They might be tourists, as they're holding a map.
de.q: Stell dir ein Foto von Leuten vor, die am Tisch lachen. Wer könnten sie sein, und was feiern sie vielleicht?
de.c: Nimm ein beliebiges Bild und schreib vier Vermutungen mit might, must, can't und looks like, jeweils mit Grund.

en.g: Talk about films, give short reviews and make recommendations.
p: Describe the plot in the present simple: It's set in Tokyo. It's about a chef who loses his sense of taste.
Strong opinion words: gripping, moving, hilarious, predictable, overrated. The acting is superb. The ending is a letdown.
Recommend: It's well worth watching. I'd highly recommend it to anyone who likes sci-fi. Don't miss it!
en.q: What's the best film you've seen recently? What's it about, and would you recommend it?
en.c: Recommend a film to me in four sentences: setting, plot without spoilers, one strong adjective and who would love it.

de.g: Du sprichst über Filme, gibst kurze Kritiken und Empfehlungen.
p: Die Handlung im present simple: It's set in Tokyo. It's about a chef who loses his sense of taste.
Starke Meinungswörter: gripping, moving, hilarious, predictable, overrated. The acting is superb. The ending is a letdown.
Empfehlen: It's well worth watching. I'd highly recommend it to anyone who likes sci-fi. Don't miss it!
de.q: Was ist der beste Film, den du in letzter Zeit gesehen hast? Worum geht es, und würdest du ihn empfehlen?
de.c: Empfiehl mir einen Film in vier Sätzen: Ort, Handlung ohne Spoiler, ein starkes Adjektiv und für wen er ideal ist.

es.c: Recomiéndame una película en cuatro frases: lugar, trama sin spoilers, un adjetivo fuerte y a quién le encantaría.

en.g: Write a short review of a film, book or restaurant with opinions and reasons.
p: Structure: what it is, what you liked, what you didn't like, and a final verdict with a rating.
Balance with linkers from earlier days: The food was delicious. However, the service was slow. Although it's long, it's gripping.
End clearly: On the whole, it's well worth it. I'd give it four out of five. I'd recommend it to families.
en.q: Which restaurant, book or film would you like to review? What was the highlight for you?
en.c: Write a 60-word review of a place or book: one positive, one negative with however, and a verdict out of five.

de.g: Du schreibst eine kurze Kritik über einen Film, ein Buch oder ein Restaurant, mit Meinung und Gründen.
p: Aufbau: Was es ist, was dir gefiel, was nicht, und ein Fazit mit Bewertung.
Ausgewogen mit Konnektoren: The food was delicious. However, the service was slow. Although it's long, it's gripping.
Klarer Schluss: On the whole, it's well worth it. I'd give it four out of five. I'd recommend it to families.
de.q: Welches Restaurant, Buch oder welchen Film würdest du gern bewerten? Was war für dich das Highlight?
de.c: Schreib eine Kritik mit 60 Wörtern: ein Plus, ein Minus mit however und ein Fazit mit Note von eins bis fünf.

es.g: Escribe una reseña corta de una película, un libro o un restaurante con opiniones y razones.

Equilibra con conectores: The food was delicious. However, the service was slow. Although it's long, it's gripping.
Cierra con claridad: On the whole, it's well worth it. I'd give it four out of five. I'd recommend it to families.
es.q: ¿Qué restaurante, libro o película te gustaría reseñar? ¿Qué fue lo mejor para ti?
es.c: Escribe una reseña de 60 palabras: algo positivo, algo negativo con however y un veredicto sobre cinco.

fr.c: Écris une critique de 60 mots : un point positif, un négatif avec however et un verdict sur cinq.
